newsitem.title: USA: Koch Gateway plans to expand Texas natgas pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Koch Gateway plans to expand Texas natgas pipeline.

text.p: Koch Gateway Pipeline Co said it plans to increase its natural gas pipeline capacity in east Texas to reduce transport constraints into the northern Louisiana market in time for the 1998-1999 winter.
The company said it will increase firm transportation capacity by 150 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) for deliveries to Perryville, La., customers from Carthage, Texas.
"This project gives East Texas producers and shippers an inexpensive, reliable outlet for increasing supplies in the area," Koch's president Dan Stecklein said in statement.
Customers affected by the project will be Texas Gas Transmission, Texas Eastern Transmission, Mississippi River Transmission, Tennessee Gas Pipeline, Southern Natural and NorAm Gas Transmission.
The project involves the construction of a new mainline interconnect with Texas Gas and a new supply lateral from the Carthage Hub.
Compression will also be added in the Perryville area and at the Carthage Junction, Hall Summit and Clarence compressor stations.
Environmental studies are currently underway, and Koch plans to file its plans with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission in early 1997.
Koch Gateway is a unit of Koch Industries Inc
